text: The mark beneath the linen pulsed once. He froze.
speaker: Narrator

text: Not toward north. Not toward the ground. For a single instant it pointed toward the journal. Then it spun and settled downward again.
speaker: Narrator

text: Below him, somewhere deep beneath the city, there was a sound. It was not loud. It was not even clearly a sound. More like a pressure moving through stone.
speaker: Narrator

text: The roof beneath Zik's hand gave a faint vibration. He remained perfectly still.
speaker: Narrator

text: The city continued around him. A donkey brayed. Someone shouted in the street. A child began crying.
speaker: Narrator

text: When sleep finally took him, he dreamed of black water moving around his ankles in a chamber he had never seen. Somewhere in the dark, something was writing—slow strokes, patient, one after another. A voice behind him said a name he had never heard.
speaker: Narrator

text: He woke with the taste of that water still in his mouth. The mark under the linen was warm.
speaker: Narrator

text: Below the floor, a single knock.
speaker: Narrator

text: Zik sat up. The sound did not come again.
speaker: Narrator

text: He reached for his father's journal.
speaker: Narrator
